description: Networked agent-based model of behavioral adoption driven by peer influence, media signals, and policy interventions. Agents (persons) on a contact network decide daily whether to adopt a behavior (e.g., technology, health practice) via a logistic hazard informed by neighbors' adoption, media intensity, policy level, and individual heterogeneity and fatigue.

modules.name: NetworkBuilder
modules.description: Constructs the static contact network using a configuration model with tunable degree heterogeneity and adds clustering via triadic closure.

notes: Uses a lognormal degree distribution parameterized by mean_degree and degree_cv.
configuration_model_from_degree_sequence should correct for multi-edges/self-loops by rewire or rejection.
Runs only at t=0; subsequent ticks are no-ops.

modules.name: MediaBroadcast
modules.description: Generates daily media signal intensity via an AR(1) process with occasional shocks.

notes: Stationary AR(1) with |phi|<1 enforced via bounds.
Shocks capture sudden news cycles or virality.

modules.name: PolicyModule
modules.description: Schedules policy level and incentives over time with a ramp-up after activation.

update_rule.pseudocode:
if t < policy_activation_day:
  raw_level = 0.0
else:
  x = (t - policy_activation_day) / max(1, policy_ramp_days)
  raw_level = policy_level_max * min(1.0, max(0.0, x))
policy_level = enforcement_strength * raw_level
signal.policy.level[t] = policy_level
signal.policy.incentive[t] = incentive_amount
notes: Allows both enforcement_strength and incentive_amount to shape effective policy pressure.
Ramp produces a smooth transition rather than a step change.

modules.name: SocialInfluence
modules.description: Agent-level adoption decision based on peers, media, policy, costs, fatigue, and heterogeneity.

update_rule.pseudocode:
events = []
for each person i:
  person.i.adopted_today = False
for each person i where person.i.adopted == False:
  neighbors = neighbors_of(i)
  active_neighbors = [j in neighbors where Bernoulli(contact_activation_prob) == 1]
  if len(active_neighbors) == 0:
    peer_share = 0.0
  else:
    peer_share = mean(person.j.adopted for j in active_neighbors)
  media = signal.media.intensity[t]
  policy = signal.policy.level[t]
  # Utility with heterogeneity and costs
  U = base_adoption_logit 
      + peer_effect * peer_share 
      + media_effect * media 
      + policy_effect * policy 
      - cost_sensitivity * person.i.adoption_threshold 
      + fatigue_effect * person.i.fatigue 
      + person.i.propensity_intercept
  # Logistic probability with noise
  p = sigmoid(U + Normal(0, noise_scale))
  if Bernoulli(p) == 1:
    person.i.adopted = True
    person.i.adopted_today = True
    events.append(i)
  # Update fatigue regardless of adoption outcome
  person.i.fatigue = person.i.fatigue * fatigue_decay + fatigue_increment_per_day_under_policy * policy
signal.adoption.events[t] = events
notes: propensity_intercept ~ Normal(0, heterogeneity_propensity_std) is drawn at initialization per agent.
fatigue reduces adoption propensity when fatigue_effect < 0.
contact_activation_prob induces day-to-day variation in exposure.

modules.name: AdoptionAggregator
modules.description: Aggregates individual adoption states into daily observables and optionally smooths time series.

update_rule.pseudocode:
N = init.population_size
new_count = len(signal.adoption.events[t])
adopted_rate = mean(person.i.adopted for all persons i)
cumulative = round(adopted_rate * N)
# Optional simple moving average smoothing for reporting
w = max(1, smoothing_window_days)
observable.new_adoptions_daily[t] = moving_average_over_window(new_count, w)
observable.adoption_rate_daily[t] = moving_average_over_window(adopted_rate, w)
observable.cumulative_adopters[t] = moving_average_over_window(cumulative, w)
notes: moving_average_over_window applies centered or trailing average; implement trailing for causality.
Outputs are aligned daily with SocialInfluence updates.

algorithms.configuration_model_with_closure: Builds a simple-graph configuration model from a target degree sequence and increases clustering via probabilistic triadic closure.
algorithms.ar1_with_shocks: AR(1) process s_t = mu*(1-phi) + phi*s_{t-1} + eps_t, with Bernoulli(p_shock) additive Gaussian shock.
algorithms.logistic_hazard_adoption: Daily adoption probability p = sigmoid(U + eps), where U combines peer share, media, policy, costs, fatigue, and heterogeneity.
